excludes: rich rendering — scene (3D) surfaces are not rendered; a view is presented as its text (`data`) fallback and, for screen surfaces, as a terminal cell grid

media — audio surfaces and image rendering are not presented, including the intent/byte image protocol sketched in issue #1071: it needs frame kinds the contract does not name, which the F11.12 gate reserves to a contract revision (v2 outline, non-goals)

provider offers — no F13.7 capability providers are declared or answered; no provider is named for the TUI in issue #1071, the v2 outline, or issue #12818, and provider_request frames are not presented

world hosting and program authoring — the browser shell's install_begin/install_chunk/install_end and compile frames are not sent; the TUI is a world-session client, not a hosting or authoring surface
offline reading — not claimed; that is the browser shell's slice-1 surface (issue #10927). The TUI presents a live session, locally hosted or remote
agent-profile surfaces — semantic_diff and screen_subscription frames are not presented; the TUI's screen read is the view frame, as in the browser shell
posture: local-first: the shell is a presentation client of a world host — a local host when one is running, otherwise a remote host reached directly over iroh; it hosts no world and implements no hosted or quota surface

presentation.error: not presented as content: an error frame refuses the session and surfaces as a session failure
presentation.events: presented in the chat panel and folded into the room/object selector (chat_posted, region_changed, object_changed, input_applied, program_changed, system_event)
presentation.screen: terminal cell grid (ratatui): the view frame's screen surface rendered as styled terminal cells, with patch negotiation on join as in the browser shell
presentation.surface_less_view: the legacy `data` text fallback, the same rule the terminal shell presents
presentation.text_and_form: deterministic text projection across three panels (room/object selector, room/document, chatroom — issue #1071); form surfaces render as text panels with their actions, answered with form_result

reconnect: reconnect presents the last applied sequence and the session's history identity (join `after` / `resume_token`); where continuity cannot be established the shell takes a fresh snapshot — divergence resolves by re-snapshot, never by merge (the v1 history-identity rule)
recorded_for: shells v2 slice 2 (issue #12818); terms per doc/2026-11-23T03-17-14Z_design_more_shells_v2 (issue #6297), section 2 and decision D3 — the claimed subset, recorded before implementation starts
